issues.title: Cross-field validation uses field validator
issues.description: The rule requires cross-field validation to use @model_validator decorator, but the code uses @field_validator which accesses unvalidated fields via info.data, causing order-dependent validation issues
issues.rule_name: Pydantic Models Must Use model_validator for Cross-Field Validation

issues.title: Incorrect automation_triggered_event_id for state-specific actions
issues.description: When actions_on_trigger or actions_on_resolve are executed, they should be linked to their specific triggered_event.id or resolved_event.id respectively. However, the code incorrectly uses primary_state_change_event_id (which always prefers Triggered over Resolved) for both types of actions. This breaks the tracing chain for actions_on_resolve - they will reference the wrong event ID when only a Resolved state change occurs, making it impossible to correctly trace the action back to the automation.resolved event that actually prompted it.

issues.title: Missing related resources in action.triggered event on failure path
issues.description: In the fail() method, the code builds related_resources list that includes both automation-triggered-event and triggering-event references. However, when emitting the 'prefect.automation.action.triggered' event, it incorrectly uses self._resulting_related_resources instead of the newly built related_resources list. This means the action.triggered event will not include the automation-triggered-event or triggering-event links on the failure path, breaking the traceability chain documented in the PR. Users won't be able to trace from failed actions back to their source events.

                    resource=resource,

issues.title: Validation incorrectly rejects proactive triggers with automation_triggered_event_id
issues.description: The field_validator for automation_triggered_event_id prevents setting this field when triggering_event is None. However, proactive triggers (which have no triggering_event) still create automation.triggered events and need to link actions to them via automation_triggered_event_id. The code in triggers.py sets automation_triggered_event_id=primary_state_change_event_id for all actions including proactive triggers, causing Pydantic validation to fail at runtime. This breaks all proactive automations, which is a critical functional regression.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #20227 - Link automation.action.* events to automation.triggered event

structured_output.summary:
This PR adds an `automation_triggered_event_id` field to `TriggeredAction`. `triggers.act()` fills it with the ID of the `automation.triggered` (or `automation.resolved`) event, and `Action.succeed()`/`Action.fail()` use it to add a related resource with the role `automation-triggered-event` to the action events. The PR also cleans up `succeed()` so it reuses the `resource` it already builds, and adds the `triggering-event` link to the `executed`/`failed` events.

The idea is good, but two bugs block merge. First, the new validator rejects `automation_triggered_event_id` whenever `triggering_event` is None. `act()` always sets the ID, so a proactive automation with no matching event now raises a `ValidationError` inside `act()` and none of its actions are published. I reproduced this against the head commit. Second, in `fail()` the `related=` arguments were swapped the wrong way. The `action.triggered` event on the failure path now carries only `_resulting_related_resources`, so it loses both the old `triggering-event` link and the new link. The PR's own `test_failure_events_include_automation_triggered_event_link` asserts that link on `triggered_event`, so that test should fail.
structured_output.verdictRationale: The new validator breaks proactive automations that have no triggering event, so no actions get published for them. `fail()` also drops related resources from `action.triggered`, which is a regression and contradicts the PR's own test. Both must be fixed before merge.

architecture.overview:
When a trigger fires, `triggers.act()` builds one state-change event (`prefect.automation.triggered` or `.resolved`) for each trigger state and publishes them. It then builds a `TriggeredAction` for every action in `automation.actions`, `actions_on_trigger` and `actions_on_resolve`, and puts each one on the actions queue. The actions service reads each `TriggeredAction`, runs it, and calls `Action.succeed()` or `Action.fail()`. Each of those emits an `action.triggered` event followed by an `action.executed` or `action.failed` event.

This PR passes the state-change event's ID through that pipeline. `act()` picks a primary state-change event (Triggered first, then Resolved) and stores its ID on every `TriggeredAction` as `automation_triggered_event_id`. A new validator requires `triggering_event` to be set whenever that ID is set. `succeed()`/`fail()` then add an `automation-triggered-event` related resource alongside the existing `triggering-event` one.
steps: Start at `triggers.act()` (src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py ~425): it builds and publishes `state_change_events`, one per trigger state.
The new code picks `primary_state_change_event_id` (Triggered first, then Resolved) and adds it as a third element of each `source_actions` tuple.
Each tuple becomes a `TriggeredAction` with the new `automation_triggered_event_id` field. The `field_validator` in schemas/automations.py rejects the ID when `triggering_event` is None.
The actions service deserializes the `TriggeredAction` and runs the action.

`Action.succeed()`/`Action.fail()` (src/prefect/server/events/actions.py) build `related_resources`: the action's own resources, then `automation-triggered-event`, then `triggering-event`. Both emitted events should carry that list.

findings.title: Validator breaks proactive automations that have no triggering event
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/schemas/automations.py` (lines ~772-780), the new `validate_automation_triggered_event_id` field_validator rejects `automation_triggered_event_id` when `triggering_event` is None. `triggers.act()` (src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py ~440-489) always sets that ID, so proactive automations with no triggering event raise a ValidationError and publish no actions. Remove the validator. The automation.triggered event exists independently of the triggering event. Then add a test in `tests/events/server/triggers/test_service.py` asserting that for a proactive firing without a triggering_event, the published TriggeredAction has a non-None `automation_triggered_event_id`.

findings.title: fail() emits action.triggered without the related resources
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/actions.py`, inside `Action.fail()` (around line 202), the `prefect.automation.action.triggered` event is emitted with `related=self._resulting_related_resources`. Change it to `related=related_resources` so it includes the `automation-triggered-event` and `triggering-event` links, matching `succeed()` and the previous behavior. Then run `tests/events/server/actions/test_actions_service.py::test_failure_events_include_automation_triggered_event_link` to confirm it passes.

findings.title: actions_on_resolve link to the Triggered event, not the Resolved event
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/prefect/server/events/triggers.py` `act()` (lines ~459-471), `actions_on_trigger` and `actions_on_resolve` entries use `primary_state_change_event_id` (which prefers Triggered), so resolve actions link to the wrong state-change event when both states are present. Use `triggered_event.id` for `actions_on_trigger` and `resolved_event.id` for `actions_on_resolve`. Keep `primary_state_change_event_id` only for the default `automation.actions`.

findings.title: test_service assertions can't detect a missing or wrong automation_triggered_event_id
findings.fixPrompt: In `tests/events/server/triggers/test_service.py`, the reactive and proactive `test_acting_publishes_an_action_message_*` tests set `automation_triggered_event_id=parsed.automation_triggered_event_id` in the expected TriggeredAction, which makes the check tautological. Capture the automation.triggered event passed to the patched `messaging.publish` and assert `parsed.automation_triggered_event_id` equals its `id` (and is not None), for both the reactive and proactive cases.

findings.title: succeed() now reuses its resource and links triggering-event on executed/failed events
findings.body: `succeed()` used to build the automation `Resource` inline twice and ignore the `resource` it had already built. That meant `prefect.posture` was missing from `action.triggered`/`action.executed` for event triggers. Reusing `resource` fixes that. Adding the `triggering-event` link to the `executed`/`failed` events also makes tracing more consistent, and the per-action test updates cover it well.
